text: 固定入力から実行・検証 周期正弦波の線形移流：風上法と解析解 周期正弦波の輸送を解析的な平行移動と比べ、格子細分化・平均値保存・最大値原理を確認する。 長さ1の周期区間でq_t+a q_x=0を1周期進め、64/128点の1次風上法を平行移動した正弦波と比較する。計算値、解析値、誤差をCSVへ出す。 手法・式・図・参照解 前提一定速度a=1、平均1、振幅0.2、基本モード。既存difference_stepを前進Eulerで呼び、実際の|C|≤0.5になる等間隔時間刻みを使う。入力で速度・正弦波・区間・格子を指定できるが、非ゼロ速度、正振幅、十分なモード解像とCFL条件を検査する。単位x・時間・移流量qは無次元。速度は区間長/時間、Courant数は無次元。境界・モデルの範囲np.rollによる周期境界。平均値保存と初期標本の値域を超えないことを別々に検査する。 EXECUTION · VALIDATION Periodic sine advection: upwind and analytic transport Compare periodic sine transport with analytic translation; check refinement, mean conservation and the maximum principle. Advance q_t+a q_x=0 for one period on a unit periodic interval. Compare first-order upwind on 64/128 points with an analytically translated sine, exporting computed, analytic and error values. Methods, equations, figures and references AssumptionsConstant speed a=1, mean 1, amplitude 0.2 and the fundamental mode. Existing difference_step is called with forward Euler and equal time steps with actual |C|≤0.5. Inputs expose the speed, sine, interval and grids, with nonzero speed, positive amplitude, mode resolution and CFL checks.Unitsx, time and transported scalar q are nondimensional; speed is interval length/time and the Courant number is dimensionless.Boundaries and model scopePeriodic boundaries via np.roll. Mean conservation and preservation of the initial sampled range are checked separately. Inputs and execution Fixed input / recipes/advection-sine.json Run from: atlas-code-2026-11-22 (the edition directory inside the extracted ZIP) python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/advection-sine.json --output output-advection-sineTests and dependency filespython -m pytest -q tests/test_recipes.py core / requirements.txt testing / requirements.txt plotting / requirements.txt Inspect outputs, acceptance and citation Generated files and reference outputs result.json (JSON) · Packaged reference output solution.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output Reference type and comparison CSV contains one row per fine-grid center, with the analytic reference evaluated at exactly the same time and location.
